A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 19-page versions of CreditDecoding, including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–19 are identical; first-page differences are confined to affiliations and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original CreditDecoding benchmark results in Tables 1–3, plus ablations, decoding-trace analyses and throughput measurements in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, decoding-trace analyses and throughput measurements reported in v2.

M1.justification: The trace-credit update, logit fusion, tuning-free schedule, Algorithm 1 and full-distribution variant in Appendix C.8 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight benchmarks and retain the same long-generation scenarios and task coverage throughout the main text and appendices.

E2.justification: The baseline and Fast-dLLM comparisons, decoding strategies in Table 3, and optimization combinations in Table 5 retain identical comparator membership.

E3.justification: All reported settings are unchanged, including main-experiment generation length 256, block size 64, early stopping, model configurations, and the metrics and in-context learning settings in Appendix B.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter and block-length ablations, focused-enhancement tests, decoding-trace case studies, and failure analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C are identical.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same single-run reporting statement. Existing variability displays, including Figure 4's standard-deviation band, are unchanged; no statistical reporting is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains the LLaDA-8B CreditDecoding average score of 53.98 and TPF of 5.48, while Table 9 retains average TPS of 32.72.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, credit equations and minimum-logit-gain derivation in Appendix C.1, including Equations 8–12, are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same training-free acceleration contribution, reported performance benefits, and generality, scalability and orthogonality claims.

C2.justification: Mechanism interpretations and limitations are identical, including insufficient credit accumulation with few steps, task-dependent tuning, and reasoning-task failures discussed on page 10 and in Appendix C.11.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures are unchanged, including hardware, hyperparameters, inference frameworks, Algorithm 1 and Appendices A–B. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list and the paper's positioning relative to earlier diffusion-model and acceleration research are identical.

P1.justification: v3 removes Zhiyun Jiang's Zhejiang University affiliation and Haibo Feng's Southern University of Science and Technology affiliation, adjusts their superscripts, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Narrative text and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Removing one affiliation line shortens and slightly repositions the first-page author/affiliation block. All figures, tables, captions and subsequent page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision changes affiliation information and the first-page header layout while preserving all scientific content, evidence, explanations and limitations, including the appendices. These administrative edits provide no evidence of a meaningful overall quality gain or decline.
